name: KM3NeT
summary: A Mediterranean research infrastructure with two complementary neutrino telescopes: ARCA offshore Sicily for high-energy astronomy and ORCA offshore France for atmospheric-neutrino oscillations.
physics_targets: Cosmic neutrino sources and diffuse emission
Neutrino mass ordering and atmospheric oscillations
detection_principle: Vertical detection units carry pressure spheres containing multiple small photomultipliers. Precise photon timing reconstructs Cherenkov light from neutrino-induced tracks and cascades in seawater.

sites.name: KM3NeT-ARCA
sites.location: Ionian Sea offshore Portopalo di Capo Passero, Sicily

status.label: Multiple stages
status.evidence: Both partial arrays take data during staged construction; current official pages describe ARCA with 51 detection units and ORCA with 28 detection units.

timeline.event: KM3-230213A recorded by a partial ARCA detector.

collaboration.name: KM3NeT Collaboration
collaboration.participants_note: Institutions listed here are selected documented participants; the official collaboration page provides the complete membership.

key_parameters.name: ARCA design
key_parameters.value: Two blocks of 115 detection units; approximately 1 km³ total instrumented volume

key_parameters.name: ORCA design
key_parameters.value: One dense block of 115 detection units for GeV-scale atmospheric neutrinos

key_parameters.name: Optical module
key_parameters.value: 31 small photomultiplier tubes per digital optical module

key_parameters.name: Site depths
key_parameters.value: Approximately 3,500 m for ARCA; 2,450 m for ORCA

key_parameters.name: Currently documented partial arrays
key_parameters.value: ARCA51 and ORCA28 on the official project pages; the 230/115-unit arrays remain the full KM3NeT 2.0 designs.

phases.name: ARCA
phases.description: Sparse offshore-Italian array optimised for TeV–PeV neutrino astronomy.

phases.name: ORCA
phases.description: Dense offshore-French array optimised for GeV atmospheric-neutrino physics.

results.summary: KM3-230213A was interpreted as an exceptionally energetic cosmic neutrino; the estimated neutrino energy is around 220 PeV with substantial uncertainty.
Partial arrays already support atmospheric-neutrino and astrophysical analyses while construction continues.

science_scope: Parameters refer to the named apparatus or explicitly identified design phase. Projections describe sensitivity goals and are not observations.
